subject: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 regression — kernel eviction / GPU mem fragmentation traces
messages:
From: liam.oneill@acmesoftware.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency spikes this morning (p95/p99)

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 and p99 latency on the Hosted API integration at ~07:45 PDT. End-users report slow responses and a couple of 503s. Our logs show a cluster of OOM-related errors and long tail latencies for token generation requests to model: open-gpt-70b-v2.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? We rely on the posted latency SLA; this is affecting a live promo. I've attached a short trace export.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
SRE Manager, Acme Software

Attachments: acme-trace-20260411.log (log fragment)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: liam.oneill@acmesoftware.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes this morning (p95/p99)

Hi Liam — thanks for the trace. We're looking immediately.

Initial telemetry shows coordinated p95/p99 regressions across the Hosted API region (us-west-2) starting 07:40–07:50. A narrow subset of GPU pods serving the open-gpt-70b-v2 variant reported repeated kernel eviction events and short-lived OOMs; that matches the OOM signatures you're seeing.

Immediate actions:
- I've asked runtime on-call to pull heap snapshots + kernel eviction logs (cc Rishi).
- We're routing new requests to a compatible lower-memory variant (open-gpt-70b-v2-quant) to reduce OOMs while we debug.

Will update with a concrete mitigation timeline. Sorry for the disruption — we know this is high impact.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes this morning (p95/p99)

TL;DR: runtime seeing fragmentation-driven evictions + transient OOMs on a small subset of older GPU instances. Rolling kernel patch and / or restart recommended for impacted pools.

Details:
- Observed behavior: repeated kernel-level memory eviction events (driver-level) correlated with GC-like host-side spikes. Memory never goes to a single massive allocation OOM; instead we see fragmentation causing failed allocations for KV cache growth during long-context requests.
- Scope: ~12 pods (~3% of serving fleet for that model) across two racks.
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 for affected customer routes; overall throughput throttled when autoscaler tried to compensate.

Immediate mitigations performed:
1) Traffic steering: moved Acme routes to quantized variants (result: ~60% reduction in p99 for their traffic).
2) Draining: we started rolling drains of affected pods and re-provisioning onto newer instance families with a kernel memory patch queued.
3) Cache policy tweak: temporarily lowered multiplier for prefix KV cache growth to avoid large allocations.

We'll have kernel patch + controlled rolling restart plan in the next 2–4 hours. We'll also provide trace artifacts and recommended customer credits once we stabilize.

-Rishi
Engineering Lead, Runtime

2) We need a more detailed artifact bundle (heap snapshot and allocation timeline) for our incident review.

Appreciate the traffic steering — the quantized variant is stable so far.

-Liam

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, liam.oneill@acmesoftware.com
Date: 2026-04-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes this morning (p95/p99) — mitigation and post-mortem plan

Update for all:

- Status: Incident mitigated as of 15:40 PDT on 2026-04-12. We completed a controlled roll of the affected racks onto instances with the patched driver and increased slab compaction settings; the kernel patch reduced fragmentation-related allocation failures.
- Customer impact: Acme saw p99 regressions for ~6 hours total (07:40–13:50 PDT), largely concentrated in the morning traffic burst. Quant variant fallback prevented a larger outage.
- Artifacts: uploaded allocation traces and heap snapshots to the incident ticket (link below). See attached stub: gpu-heap-snapshot-stub.txt.

Next steps / Post-mortem scope:
1) Deep analysis of allocation patterns that triggered fragmentation (open ticket INF-4921).
2) Evaluate proactive health checks to detect kernel eviction patterns earlier and auto-evacuate pods.
3) Provide Acme a 1-day service credit and schedule a joint post-mortem review next week.

Apologies again to the Acme team. We'll follow up with the full PM notes and remediation timeline.

-Rishi
Engineering Lead, Runtime
